Definition: to seize by the heel; figuratively, to circumvent (as if tripping up the heels); also to restrain (as if holding by the heel)
BiblicalUsage: The word means to take by the heel, and it is Jacob's story in a single verb. Esau says his brother is rightly named Jacob, for he has supplanted him twice; Jeremiah warns that every brother will utterly supplant his neighbour; and Hosea looks back to the womb, where Jacob took his brother by the heel before he had done anything at all.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jacob's name tells the truth about all of us: we grab for the blessing with our own hands before we learn to receive it. God did not change Jacob by renaming him first; He wrestled with him until the supplanter became Israel.
